brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Seamline, the open-source command-line tool in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: precise, trustworthy, developer-native; it must work in a terminal-heavy README, as a GitHub avatar and on a small docs site. No database cylinders, no elephants, no generic terminal prompt. Web and GitHub only.

claim.notes: Beş konseptin hiçbiri kalite kapısını geçmedi (üçü kapıda başarısız, ikisi eskiz incelemesinde elendi), bu yüzden finalize, export, install-assets ve gallery çalıştırılmadı.

concepts.title: Planned vs Applied
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 stop button / checked checkbox; s2 pagination or loading dots, 2x2 app grid; s3 pie chart (also a Mercedes/radiation-like tri-split); s4 pinwheel of four bars, a crop or fullscreen icon; s5 split diagonal square, the contrast icon. All five are struck: UI state glyphs or stock geometry. The solid-vs-hollow-twin device will always read as a UI state (filled vs empty, done vs pending) wherever it goes, so another arrangement of it will not reach distinctiveness 6. Drop the device and try a different move: one specific ownable silhouette that comes from the name (seam + line), drawn as an object, not a state indicator. No grids of dots, no frames, no pies, no diagonal splits.

concepts.title: Lane Handover
readsAs: two parallel lightning-bolt jogs (unfortunate: close to the paired sig-rune 'SS' silhouette)
slanted closing double quotation mark or a 'layout shift' UI glyph
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a stepped pipe or 'Z'/'2' glyph, Tetris-like; s2 a drag-handle UI icon or domino dots at 16px; s3 a square sliced diagonally with the half offset (stock sliced-block device, 62% stock similarity); s4 a two-rail track or box-drawing double line that jogs one lane sideways without breaking. Keep s4: it is closest to the idea (the shift happens with traffic still flowing) and the double-line feel is developer-native (like box-drawing characters ║╝). Risks: it can read as a generic pipe fitting or road symbol, and the jog currently looks like a ⅃ hook. Fix: make the jog a clear diagonal or a precisely radiused offset so both rails stay parallel and continuous, with equal rail and gap widths at 16px (right now the gap closes up), and check it doesn't turn into an 'H' or 'll'. Green is good; keep it off cyan.

concepts.title: Plan Stitch
readsAs: a dashed 'cut here' line crossed by one bar
a magic wand / sparkle stick at 16 px
amber-and-black caution/construction tape (unfortunate for a safety tool: reads as warning)
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a diagonal dotted trail that ends in a dark bar crossing it (a motion trail, or a plan ending in a commit); s2 a broken-chain 'unlink' UI icon / no-entry sign (78% stock similarity); s3 sewing stitches or a scar/zipper, a literal sewing cliché that gets busy at 16px; s4 climbing bars that read as a signal-strength or chart icon, with a cursor; s5 a sliced square with one half offset (sliced-shape device). Keep s1: planned steps along a seam, then the one that is executed, which fits 'shows what will happen before it happens'. Risks: the dots shrink in size, so it reads as a comet or motion trail, and at 16px the small dots disappear (the tab render is just a blur). Fix: use equal-length dash stitches on one clear diagonal axis, no more than 3, with the final bar truly crossing the seam line instead of capping it, and weight them so 16px keeps the dashes. Ochre and black are distinctive in the category; keep them.

concepts.title: Drawn Word
readsAs: the letters 'Li' (lithium) or 'Ui' as a monogram
a U-shaped cup/bracket with a dot beside it
in the word, 'seamUne'/'seamLine' with a capital-L glitch — unfortunate: 'UI' for a CLI tool, or a generic Li-ion battery label
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a stock geometric single-storey a, and the seam gap is invisible; s2 an m with uneven arches, which at 16 px reads as 'hn' or 'rn' and carries no seam idea; s3 'li' drawn as one J/U stroke with a square dot, the closest to its idea and the lowest stock similarity (38%); s4 a generic gapped e in the Enel family, struck. s1 and s4 are struck; s2 is weak. s3 is picked, with risks. (1) In the word, an l joined to an i at the baseline can read as a 'u', giving 'seamune': test the full lowercase wordmark first and keep the l's ascender clearly above x-height and the i's dot clearly separate. (2) Alone, the symbol reads as a hook, pipe or paperclip end. Make the baseline turn a crisp ruled corner or a tight radius drawn like a ruled line, not a soft U, so it reads as one line being drawn. (3) Do not let it read as a cursor or caret. The square dot must not look like a blinking block cursor beside a bar, which the brief bans.

concepts.title: The Joined Word
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s5 a black m followed by an orange text cursor (m| typed in a terminal), the dev-tool caret cliche, the thread-through-cloth idea does not read and at 16 px it is just m plus a red bar; s6 the plain glyph pair 'ml' with a small orange tab, a lowercase abbreviation in a stock font with no hook; s7 the letters 'in', which reads as LinkedIn's 'in' at once (known-logo strike), and the shared stem is invisible because i+n always share it. All three are seven-sketch variations of letters from the name touching; the wordmark-ligature route is used up. Different move: drop the letterforms and draw the seam itself as a non-letter object, e.g. two flat planes or edges meeting at one stitched line or a single line that crosses a fold, with the join as the one thing you see, then let the wordmark carry the name.
